text:
anya: quick Q — we have a customer on private deployment hitting 502s when using a custom base_url + corporate forward proxy. They set SDK baseUrl to https://private.redwood.example and tunnel+mtls is fine, but backend complains about Host header mismatch. anyone seen this?
liam: yup, seen similar. proxy rewrites Host to the proxy host unless you force passthrough. is this an http CONNECT proxy or an http-forwarding proxy?
anya: it's an outbound HTTP proxy (forwarding) that rewrites headers. the customer can't change it.
sam: if proxy rewrites Host you can set the request Host explicitly in the SDK client (some languages allow an override) or use the :authority pseudo-header for HTTP/2. which SDK are they using?
anya: Node SDK (latest). they tried setting baseUrl but didn't touch headers.
maria: in node you can pass a custom agent and set headers on each request. example quickly:```js
const client = new Redwood({ baseUrl: 'https://private.redwood.example', agent: customAgent, headers: { host: 'private.redwood.example' } })
```but note Node's http.Agent won't override Host on CONNECT — depends on proxy.
liam: another approach: use SNI to route (TLS server_name). For TLS over proxy, SNI is preserved if proxy uses CONNECT. But with forwarding proxies doing TLS termination, it's hairy.
anya: customer says proxy terminates TLS and re-encrypts, so SNI won't help. they need Host preserved in the upstream request.
sam: can we add a client option to always send an extra header x-rw-intended-host: <host> and then have the private control plane accept it as authoritative for routing? that might be safer than relying on Host mutation.
maria: that seems reasonable for Private deployments only. but we'd need to document it and add a small compatibility shim on the agent/server to prefer x-rw-intended-host when present + signed via mTLS cert tie. security ok?
anya: customer ok with x-header if it's validated. are we already capturing client cert CN on the control plane?
devex-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary rollout for private control-plane header-acceptance started (rollout-id: canary/pcp-header-2026-03). Monitor /deploys/pcp-header.
liam: we should add an opt-in flag in the SDK like { preserveUpstreamHost: true } that adds the header and also signs it (HMAC) with the client key so the control plane can verify. avoids being accidental open.
sam: agree. impl notes: Node + Python SDKs both need: header key, sign function, and opt-in param. server side will verify HMAC with registered client key metadata.
maria: I'll draft a small spec in the infra repo. tagging @anya for customer follow-up.
anya: thanks — I'll tell them it's a viable workaround and follow up once spec is ready. :thumbsup:
liam: quick sanity check for others — for anyone debugging proxy host issues: 1) test curl with -v and inspect Host, 2) test via an environment-local forward proxy to see behavior, 3) try CONNECT vs direct TLS. small checklist helps.
anya: adding that checklist to the ticket. good thread.
maria: will put a short note in the Private deployment docs about header workaround and caveats.
anya: ack, closing for now.
